::: {#fig-qp-equality-fails}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: qp-equality-fails-fig-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Graph of the value of f along the constraint line x1 equals 1, against
#|   x2 from -3 to 3. The blue curve is a downward-opening parabola with its
#|   peak of 0.5 at x2 equal to 0, and it falls without bound on both sides,
#|   so it has no lowest point.
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 5
qf_x2_qf <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 201)
qf_curve_qf <- tibble::tibble(x2 = qf_x2_qf, f = 0.5 * (1 - qf_x2_qf^2))
ggplot2::ggplot(qf_curve_qf, ggplot2::aes(x2, f)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x2", y = "f(1, x2)")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: qp-equality-fails-fig-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Graph of the value of f along the constraint line x1 equals 1, against
#|   x2 from -3 to 3. The blue curve is a downward-opening parabola with its
#|   peak of 0.5 at x2 equal to 0, and it falls without bound on both sides,
#|   so it has no lowest point.
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 5
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

qf_x2_ax = np.linspace(-3, 3, 201)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(qf_x2_ax, 0.5 * (1 - qf_x2_ax**2), color="#0072B2")
ax.set_xlabel("x2")
ax.set_ylabel("f(1, x2)")
plt.show();
```

:::

The first case of @exm-qp-equality-fails:
along the constraint $x_1 = 1$, the [value](functions.qmd#def-value) $f(1, x_2)$ falls without [bound](sets.qmd#def-bound) as $\abs{x_2}$ grows,
so there is no [minimizer](algebra.qmd#def-global-minimizer) when $\matr{S}$ is not [positive definite](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite).

:::
